body.purpose: Default UI text: descriptions, comments, values.

label.purpose: Metadata and data values in Geist Mono. Used sparingly, not as default section decoration.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Small floating/interactive elements above host-page content: widget launcher, dropped pin marker.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, popovers, the comment-entry card — anything that blocks the rest of the page.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default hover/press/state transitions (buttons, launcher, focus rings).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one non-accent-coloured interactive element by design: Ink fill, Page text. Used for the single primary action on a screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--ink); color: var(--page); border: none; border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 16px; font: 500 0.875rem/1.4 Geist, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 180ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-2); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary/tertiary action: bordered, Surface background. Used for every non-primary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 16px; font: 500 0.875rem/1.4 Geist, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 180ms ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--surface-2); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-2); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: One discrete, glanceable state per row. Never stacked with sibling pills for other metadata — that metadata becomes plain text instead.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; font: 500 0.6875rem/1.3 'Geist Mono', monospace; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; } .ds-pill--open { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 18%, transparent); color: var(--accent); } .ds-pill--resolved { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--signal) 18%, transparent); color: var(--signal); }

components.name: Panel
components.description: The one card pattern in the system: flat, single border, no shadow, no nested inner card. Sub-sections are typographic, separated by a single rule line if needed — never a second bordered box.
components.html:
Connect preview

Install once for the preview site.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px; } .ds-panel-title { font: 500 0.875rem/1.4 Geist, sans-serif; color: var(--ink); margin: 0 0 4px; } .ds-panel-body { font: 400 0.75rem/1.5 Geist, sans-serif; color: var(--ink-mute); margin: 0; }

components.name: Stat Strip
components.description: Signature component: several related numbers in one flat bordered container, divided by internal rule lines — the reference pattern for 'related metrics' that replaces stacking separate metric cards.
components.html:
Pins

6

Open

5

Resolved

1
components.css: .ds-stat-strip { display: flex; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden; background: var(--surface); } .ds-stat { flex: 1; padding: 12px; border-right: 1px solid var(--line); } .ds-stat:last-child { border-right: none; } .ds-stat-label { font: 500 0.6875rem/1.3 'Geist Mono', monospace; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-soft); margin: 0; } .ds-stat-value { font: 600 0.875rem/1.4 Geist, sans-serif; color: var(--ink); margin: 4px 0 0; } .ds-stat-value--accent { color: var(--accent); } .ds-stat-value--signal { color: var(--signal); }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Label sits above the field as persistent Geist Mono text, not as a disappearing placeholder.
components.css: .ds-field { display: block; } .ds-field-label { display: block; margin-bottom: 6px; font: 500 0.6875rem/1.3 'Geist Mono', monospace; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-mute); } .ds-field-input { width: 100%; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink); font: 400 0.875rem/1.4 Geist, sans-serif; } .ds-field-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-2); outline-offset: 2px; border-color: var(--accent); }

components.name: Nav Item
components.description: Active state is a tone shift (Surface 2) plus text weight, never an accent-coloured pill or icon badge.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: block; padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: 6px; font: 400 0.8125rem/1.4 Geist, sans-serif; color: var(--ink-mute); text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-item--active { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--ink); font-weight: 500; }

narrative.overview:
Tack is a precision tool that stays out of the way until it's needed. The surface is monochrome and calm — near-white in light, near-black in dark — with exactly one accent in active use: Pin Blue, reserved for the things that are actually actionable (focus, links, selection, the pin marker itself). Nothing in the interface performs confidence; it demonstrates it, by being operational, specific, and quiet under load. A page with six open pins and a page with sixty should feel like the same calm tool, not a dashboard straining to look busy.

Tack explicitly rejects the generic-SaaS dashboard vocabulary: gradient hero panels, AI-mascot theatrics, tiny tracked-uppercase eyebrows on every section, stacked pill badges standing in for real hierarchy, and cards nested inside cards pretending to be structure. Status and metadata are typographic first — weight and colour-on-text before a pill; a pill earns its place only when it names one genuinely discrete, glanceable state, never when three or four of them compete on the same row.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome neutral base; Pin Blue is the only sustained colour, used sparingly and always with intent.
Near-black primary actions (not the accent colour) — the accent marks state, not buttons.
Flat panels with internal typographic hierarchy over stacked bordered boxes.
Geist for all UI text; Geist Mono reserved for data that benefits from fixed-width alignment — never a default label treatment.
Fixed rem type scale, not fluid — this is a working tool viewed at consistent DPI, not a marketing page.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Pin Blue is the only sustained colour in the system. If a second decorative hue shows up on a screen that isn't a functional status colour, it's off-system.

rules.name: The Ink Button Rule
rules.body: Primary actions are near-black (or near-white in dark mode), never accent-filled. The accent's job is to mark state and selection, not to fill buttons.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: No clamp(), no fluid type in the product surface. Users view the dashboard at consistent DPI in a working session; a heading that resizes with the viewport reads as unfinished, not responsive.

rules.name: The Mono-Earns-It Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono appears only where fixed-width alignment or a 'this is data' signal genuinely helps (a CSS selector, a project key, a URL, a timestamp column). It is not a default styling flourish for labels.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Rule
rules.body: A static panel — a row, a card, a sidebar — never has a box-shadow. If something needs to look 'lifted,' that's a sign it should be a modal/popover, not a card with a shadow bolted on.

dos: Do use Pin Blue for exactly one job at a time: focus, selection, links, or the pin marker — never as page decoration.
Do build primary buttons from Ink/Page, not the accent colour (The Ink Button Rule).
Do default to typography (weight, colour-on-text, a plain label) for status and metadata before reaching for a pill.
Do use one Status Pill per row when a state is genuinely discrete and glanceable.
Do build multi-metric summaries as one bordered container with internal divider lines (the Stat Strip pattern), not as separate cards.
Do keep shadows exclusively on floating/overlay elements (modals, popovers, the widget launcher) per The Floating-Only Rule.
Do use Geist Mono only where the content is genuinely data (selectors, keys, URLs, timestamps).
donts: Don't stack multiple pill badges (status + AI label + placement + priority) on a single row competing for attention — this is the 'pill badges everywhere' anti-pattern named in PRODUCT.md, and it is explicitly retired. Fold secondary metadata into plain text or a single combined label instead.

Don't nest a bordered card inside another bordered card to represent a sub-section — nested cards are always wrong. Use one flat panel with an internal rule line, or drop the border on the inner block entirely.
Don't use a tiny tracked-uppercase eyebrow pill above a section heading when the heading already says what the section is.
Don't dress up a simple state — an empty state, a single count, an 'off' toggle — in the same heavy bordered-box-plus-icon treatment used for real data.
Don't use purple/violet, gradients, or neon accents anywhere — the old Tack direction, deliberately retired.
Don't use 'AI-powered' hero copy, magic-wand framing, or AI-mascot theatrics; describe what the AI Inbox actually does in plain terms.
Don't use fluid/clamp() type sizing on product screens — fixed rem sizes only (The Fixed-Scale Rule).
Don't write vague copy that names a feeling instead of a fact ('seamless', 'powerful,' 'supercharged'). Say what happens.
